items.label: f04-last-profile
items.front: What does the profile store do when asked to delete the only remaining profile version, and what if it deletes the active one?
items.back: Deleting the last version throws (create another first). Deleting the active version among several makes the first remaining profile active.

items.label: f02-promise-queue
items.front: How does performStoreOperation serialize profile reads and writes, and why is the stored queue next.catch(() => undefined)?
items.back: Each operation chains onto a module-level promise (queue.then(execute)). The caller gets the real promise, but the queue keeps a version with errors swallowed so one failed operation cannot reject - and thereby block - every later one.

items.label: f01-native-setter
items.front: Why does filler.ts write values through Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(prototype, "value").set and then dispatch input and change events?
items.back: Framework-controlled inputs (React) track value through the element's own setter; calling the prototype's native setter and dispatching bubbling, composed input/change events makes the framework notice the change instead of reverting it.

items.label: f03-longest-skill-first
items.front: For a "Years of experience with React Native" question, why are saved skills sorted by normalized length before matching?
items.back: Longer names are tried first, so "react native" wins over "react"; the match is also whole-token (bounded by non-alphanumeric characters), so a shorter skill cannot claim a longer one's question.

items.prompt: A select labeled "Are you a US citizen authorized to work in the United States?" offers Yes/No. What does the matcher do with the saved authorization answer?

choices.text: It fills Yes: the label mentions both work authorization and the United States
It skips the field: citizenship is treated as a protected credential question
It becomes a review item: the label fails the strict US pattern and contains "citizen"
It fills the saved legallyAuthorizedUS answer: the options are an explicit yes/no pair

choices: It fills Yes: the label mentions both work authorization and the United States
It skips the field: citizenship is treated as a protected credential question
It becomes a review item: the label fails the strict US pattern and contains "citizen"
It fills the saved legallyAuthorizedUS answer: the options are an explicit yes/no pair

items.explanation: Only labels matching the anchored clearAuthorization regex qualify, and any of not/without/unable/unless/except/only/citizen/citizenship forces review.

items.prompt: Two options tabs loaded the same profile at revision 4. Tab A saves successfully. Tab B then saves with expectedRevision 4. What happens to Tab B's save?

choices.text: It throws "This profile changed in another window...": A's save bumped the revision to 5
It succeeds and silently overwrites Tab A's changes: the last write to chrome.storage wins
It succeeds: the profile is marked unconfigured until the user reviews it again
It succeeds and merges both tabs' field changes: the two tabs edited different fields

choices: It throws "This profile changed in another window...": A's save bumped the revision to 5
It succeeds and silently overwrites Tab A's changes: the last write to chrome.storage wins
It succeeds: the profile is marked unconfigured until the user reviews it again
It succeeds and merges both tabs' field changes: the two tabs edited different fields

items.explanation: Every successful non-delete mutation increments revision. update compares op.expectedRevision to the stored revision before validating or writing.

items.prompt: A form has two "Company" fields, each inside its own employment-history block, and both initially map to experienceCompany. What does mapFields return for them?

choices.text: The first field gets entry zero and the second is skipped as a duplicate of the same employer
Each field receives the profile entry at the same index as its block's position on the page
Both receive the first saved employer, as entry zero in the profile is the most recent job
Both drop to medium confidence and stay empty, as repeated history fields need manual matching

choices: The first field gets entry zero and the second is skipped as a duplicate of the same employer
Each field receives the profile entry at the same index as its block's position on the page
Both receive the first saved employer, as entry zero in the profile is the most recent job
Both drop to medium confidence and stay empty, as repeated history fields need manual matching

items.explanation: mapFields counts education/experience kinds; any kind seen more than once loses its value and becomes medium. The comment says it plainly: do not silently repeat entry zero, including the first row.

items.prompt: Filling a <select> with the value "Yes": one enabled option has text "Yes", and a different enabled option has value="yes". Which option does fillField choose?

choices.text: The option whose visible text is "Yes": value matches are a fallback when labels miss
The option whose value attribute is "yes": machine values are more stable than display labels
Whichever of the two options appears first in the list: the first match is taken
Neither: two candidate options make the choice ambiguous, so fillField refuses to fill either

choices: The option whose visible text is "Yes": value matches are a fallback when labels miss
The option whose value attribute is "yes": machine values are more stable than display labels
Whichever of the two options appears first in the list: the first match is taken
Neither: two candidate options make the choice ambiguous, so fillField refuses to fill either

items.explanation: labelMatches is computed first; matches falls back to value comparison only if labelMatches is empty. Ambiguity is judged within the chosen list (exactly one match required).

items.prompt: How does AudioRecorder.start choose the recording format and how often does it ask MediaRecorder for data?

choices.text: The browser's default type, with recorder.start(250) emitting four chunks per second
First supported of audio/webm;codecs=opus, audio/webm, audio/mp4, with start(1000) giving 1s chunks
Plain audio/mp4 for compatibility, with one blob delivered when the recording is stopped
The first supported of audio/mp4, then audio/webm, with recorder.start(10000) emitting chunks at ten-second intervals

choices: The browser's default type, with recorder.start(250) emitting four chunks per second
First supported of audio/webm;codecs=opus, audio/webm, audio/mp4, with start(1000) giving 1s chunks
Plain audio/mp4 for compatibility, with one blob delivered when the recording is stopped
The first supported of audio/mp4, then audio/webm, with recorder.start(10000) emitting chunks at ten-second intervals

items.explanation: The mime preference list is checked with MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported; the 1000 ms timeslice is what makes per-second chunk persistence possible.

It appends the saved first name: the typed text and the value are joined with a space
It overwrites the text: a high mapping is always written once it has been computed
It overwrites the text: the typed value goes into the rollback batch so Undo restores it

It overwrites the text: a high mapping is always written once it has been computed
It overwrites the text: the typed value goes into the rollback batch so Undo restores it

items.explanation: mapField already skips fields whose valueBefore is nonempty, but that is scan-time data. filler.ts checks element.value.trim() again right before writing.

items.prompt: fillField receives a mapping whose confidence is "medium" and whose value is a perfectly valid saved email. What happens?

choices.text: The value is written only if the field is marked required on the page, as medium means optional
The value is written and added to the rollback batch, so Undo can remove it if it was wrong
The value is written, but the sidebar flags it so the user can double-check it before submitting
Nothing is written, as fillField returns false for any mapping that is not high confidence

choices: The value is written only if the field is marked required on the page, as medium means optional
The value is written and added to the rollback batch, so Undo can remove it if it was wrong
The value is written, but the sidebar flags it so the user can double-check it before submitting
Nothing is written, as fillField returns false for any mapping that is not high confidence

items.explanation: The very first guard in fillField rejects confidence !== "high" (and empty values, disabled and read-only fields). Medium and low are review-only by design.

A medium review item: the profile stores a month and year, so a full date needs review
A high-confidence "2021-03": the same format that is used for type="month" inputs

A skip: EEO questions are protected personal data the extension never touches
A medium review item of kind unknown: checkbox and radio controls are left for the user
A high-confidence eeoGender mapping: the saved answer exactly matches one of the options

items.prompt: Restoring a recovery backup: which treatment do the restored profile versions receive?

choices.text: Fresh IDs with configured flags kept, and no backup is taken before the restore replaces it
Their original IDs and revisions, so any open editors keep working against them
Fresh random IDs, configured=false and revision 0, after the old data is backed up
Their original IDs, but configured is forced to false so each profile is re-reviewed

choices: Fresh IDs with configured flags kept, and no backup is taken before the restore replaces it
Their original IDs and revisions, so any open editors keep working against them
Fresh random IDs, configured=false and revision 0, after the old data is backed up
Their original IDs, but configured is forced to false so each profile is re-reviewed

items.explanation: New IDs invalidate old editors; configured=false forces review before autofill; the pre-restoration data is written to profileRecoveryBackup before profileStore is replaced.

items.prompt: The injected content script (same extension id, but its sender.url is the job site's page) sends EAM_STORE with operation action "update". How does the service worker respond?

choices.text: It refuses: "Invalid sender." Content scripts never share the extension's own id
It ignores it: the worker never calls sendResponse, so the caller times out
It refuses: "Open Manage profiles to change profile data." Other pages may only send get
It performs the update: the sender id matches the extension's own chrome.runtime.id

choices: It refuses: "Invalid sender." Content scripts never share the extension's own id
It ignores it: the worker never calls sendResponse, so the caller times out
It refuses: "Open Manage profiles to change profile data." Other pages may only send get
It performs the update: the sender id matches the extension's own chrome.runtime.id

items.explanation: The sender.id check passes for the content script; the second check requires sender.url to start with the extension origin for anything other than action "get".

items.prompt: After Autofill filled Email, the user edited that Email field by hand, then pressed Undo. What happens to the Email field?

choices.text: It reverts to the empty value it had before the fill: Undo restores every one of the filled fields
Undo is refused for the whole batch: one of its fields changed after the fill ran
It reverts to the autofilled email: that is the batch's last known state for this field
It keeps the user's edit: rollback skips entries whose value differs from what the fill wrote

choices: It reverts to the empty value it had before the fill: Undo restores every one of the filled fields
Undo is refused for the whole batch: one of its fields changed after the fill ran
It reverts to the autofilled email: that is the batch's last known state for this field
